newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says '96 budget has 14.7 bln rgt surplus.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says '96 budget has 14.7 bln rgt surplus.

text.p: Malaysia's federal government budget is expected to show a surplus of 14.71 billion ringgit in 1996 -- its fourth successive year of surpluses, the Ministry of Finance said on Friday.
The surplus in 1995 was 14.38 billion ringgit, the ministry said in its annual Economic Report.

Total revenue is expected to increase 10.9 percent in 1996 to 56.50 billion ringgit against a three percent rise in 1995 to 50.95 billion ringgit. The increases are largely attributable to higher receipts from direct taxes, particularly corporate taxes, the report said.
Revenue is projected to increase another 7.6 percent to 60.78 billion ringgit in 1997, it said.

Revenue from income taxes was expected to rise by 8.3 percent to 23.55 billion ringgit in 1997 against an 8.2 percent increase to 21.73 billion in 1996 and a 15.9 percent increase to 20.10 billion in 1995.

Revenue from corporate taxes was projected to rise 8.2 percent to 14.32 billion ringgit in 1997 after rising 13.1 percent to 13.24 billion in 1996 and 10.8 percent to 11.71 billion in 1995, the report said.
Operating expenditure in 1996 was envisaged to increase by 14.2 percent against a 4.3 percent rise in 1995, mostly due to salary hikes for civil servants, the report said.

Social services, including education, took the lion's share of spending in 1996. It accounted for 32.1 percent of expenditures, or 13.43 billion ringgit. The sector has been allocated 14.53 billlion ringgit, or almost 35 percent of spending, in 1997, the report said.

Defence and internal security accounted for 14.8 percent of expediture or 6.20 billion ringgit in 1996. That will increase to 6.34 billion ringgit or 15.2 percent of expenditures in 1997, the report said.
